It was made at Base block 29,366,975 by transaction 0x69dee05880d3369001b4541aefe445520b3770ec1a3ac4f0e77d9171ac65fc3e from 0x2cd524394a4463a4e6f1829124dccbac436c4061 (nonce 3, type 2, chainId 0x2105) to the CREATE2 deployer 0x4e59b448 with salt 0x...0850 and 22,842 bytes of init code; keccak256(0xff ++ 0x4e59b448 ++ salt ++ keccak256(init)) gives 0x4cd3be87...c0cc. Its nonce of 543 comes from a CREATE in its own runtime, not from the factory. The init code ends with five constructor words: PoolManager 0x498581ff (Base), 0x2cd52439, 0x680a9840, 0xe4b1b173 and 0x2cd52439. Running the init code in the reference interpreter (tools/opdiff/pyevm.py) with CALLER 0x4e59b448 executes no ORIGIN, CALLER, CHAINID, TIMESTAMP, NUMBER or external call, writes slot 0 (owner) and slot 9 both = 0x2cd52439 from the arguments, emits OwnershipTransferred(0, 0x2cd52439) as the mined receipt does, and returns a runtime whose SHA-256 equals the Base runtime. An eth_call from 0x...5afe to 0x4e59b448 with the original calldata returns 0x4cd3be87...c0cc on Arbitrum One (nitro v3.13.0-rc.9), Polygon (Tenderly), OP Mainnet (op-reth v2.8.1) and BNB Smart Chain (Geth v1.8.2), so any account can fill the address on all four, and the result has owner 0x2cd52439 (the account that deployed it on Base; the Base owner today is 0xe184cba6 after a transfer) and the Base PoolManager as an immutable. With that runtime and storage placed at the address by state override, beforeSwap and afterSwap called from the local PoolManager revert with 0xae18210a, NotPoolManager(), on all four networks (8 calls). So a replay leaves every swap in these pools reverting as today, gives the replaying account no role, and removal stays open because bits 9 and 8 are clear (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:203-205, 232-243).

cleared.check: Task 3: hooks among the 25 addresses that are empty on a network with a pool there and have contract code on another network, for which a replay by a stranger would give that stranger a role. Per network answer for the networks where such pools exist, and for the rest.
cleared.result: None. Every replay that works today hands owner or admin to an address fixed in the init code (0x2cd52439, 0xe911f518, 0x7fc584c5, 0xd2c70084) or to the CREATE2 deployer, or writes no storage at all; no constructor that was run reads ORIGIN, and none leaves an initializer that a first caller could take. Where the address came from a factory deployed by a plain CREATE (0x0bde0085, 0x8cad6a96, implementation 0xcc42bf29), only the original key can rebuild it and the signed transactions carry chainId 1. Per network: Ethereum yes-replayable (0x265f6a4b), no role; OP Mainnet yes-replayable (0x4cd3be87), no role; Base yes-replayable (0x6e645101, 0x1c23af28, 0xd7333956, 0x2016c0e4), no role; Unichain 0xd7333956 replayable with no role, 0x3a3a9a07, 0x74803bd5 and 0x4440854b not replayable by a stranger; World Chain, Soneium, Polygon, Avalanche, BNB Smart Chain, Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain yes-replayable (0xa6c8d751, 0xf8c3f424, 0x4cd3be87, 0x2016c0e4, 0xacca13fc), no role; Zora, Ink, Celo, X Layer, Elysium, Monad, MegaETH, Tempo and HyperEVM have no pool on an empty hook address (cycle 22 census), and Arc's one empty hook 0x53c71870...40c0 has code on no network and its pool no position. The remaining Robinhood-coded, BNB-coded and Arc-coded hooks are listed in a lead below as unknown; none of their pools holds liquidity.

cleared.check: Whether the networks derive CREATE2 addresses as Ethereum does, so that a replay lands on the same address. This is the only chain property the replay question depends on besides the presence of the factory.
cleared.result: Yes on every network tested. eth_call of an original 0x4e59b448 deployment returned the hook address recomputed locally from keccak256(0xff ++ deployer ++ salt ++ keccak256(init)) on Ethereum, OP Mainnet, Base, Unichain, World Chain, Soneium, Arbitrum One, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche and Robinhood Chain (14 eth_call runs from sender 0x...5afe, each bracketed by web3_clientVersion). CREATE addresses of 0x0bde0085 and 0x8cad6a96 recompute from sender and nonce with RLP (kk.py rlp_create). No unit of this cycle found a network with a different derivation.

cleared.check: Task 4: flagged addresses with pools on one network that are plain accounts with a nonce or have no history on another, and whether core gives any protection.
cleared.result: No hook address of the 89 that are empty or delegated somewhere is a plain account with a nonce and no code on any network: every address with a nonzero nonce has contract code or an EIP-7702 designation there (cycle 22 xchain.json, 21 networks). The seven delegated hooks (0x52bf1a80, 0xa8531805, 0x17da3aa3, 0x12c22021, 0x30a5640e, 0x8c7852bb, 0xf028a264) have pools only on networks where they are delegated, which is F-013. About 57 flagged addresses (for example 0x...0020, 0x...dead0030, 0x8000...0000, 0x444000...00c4) have nonce 0 and no code on all 21 networks. Core gives no protection on any network: initialize checks tick spacing, currency order and isValidHookAddress, which reads only the low 14 bits of the address and the fee (src/PoolManager.sol:117-126, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-127), and never reads code; whatever code later sits at the address receives the callbacks (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-160), and the return delta flags let it move amounts against the swapper (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:248-315). For an address that no factory call and no known key reaches, placing code needs a 160 bit preimage, so the only effect is the freeze already recorded in F-004.

cleared.result: No. Every signed creation found carries a chain id: 0xc3439452 (factory 0x0bde0085), 0x89200c93 (factory 0x8cad6a96) and 0x571eb206 (implementation 0xcc42bf29) are type 2 with chainId 1, 0x69dee058 and 0x795b9feb are type 2 with chainId 0x2105, and 0xcabd0c17 is legacy with v = 0x128, which is EIP-155 for chainId 130. leads.question: How were the hooks with code only on Robinhood Chain (0x28e8716a, 0x42554fa5, 0x7266ba24, 0xa1194917, 0xb64c113c, 0xbd71a7b4, 0xd995ed0b), only on BNB Smart Chain (0xa9e0db05, 0xb65fba32, 0xd60e0546, 0xd7eafeb2, 0xf8efbf01) and only on Arc (0x850ff03d) created, and would a replay on the networks where they are empty give the replaying account a role? 0xb65fba32 and 0xd60e0546 read ORIGIN in their runtime and 0xbd71a7b4 also uses CREATE2.
leads.why: The Robinhood Chain RPC refuses historical state, the Robinhood Chain and Arc explorers return a Cloudflare challenge, and the BNB Smart Chain Tenderly gateway returns 404, so the creation transactions were not found. None of the pools on these addresses holds liquidity at the cycle 22 blocks, so no funds are at stake today; a pool that gains liquidity later would make the answer matter.

leads.question: Were the EIP-7702 authorizations that delegate the hook accounts 0x52bf1a80, 0xa8531805, 0x17da3aa3, 0x12c22021, 0x30a5640e, 0x8c7852bb and 0xf028a264 signed with chain_id 0? A chain_id 0 authorization with nonce 0 can be submitted by anyone on any network where the account still has nonce 0.
leads.why: Such a replay sets the same delegate on a new network without the key holder. No pool names these addresses on a network where they are empty today, and the delegate's code decides who controls it, so this is not a path to current funds.

leadResults.answer: Of the 25 hook addresses that are empty on a network with a pool there and have contract code elsewhere, 12 were traced to their creation. 0x4cd3be87...c0cc came through the CREATE2 deployer 0x4e59b448 (not CreateX) and anyone can replay it on Arbitrum One, Polygon, OP Mainnet and BNB Smart Chain, but the replay sets owner 0x2cd52439 from the init code and keeps the Base PoolManager as an immutable, so the local PoolManager's swap callbacks revert with NotPoolManager and the pools stay as they are. 0xa6c8d751 replays as a stateless no-op hook with no role. 0x265f6a4b, 0xd7333956, 0x2016c0e4, 0x6e645101, 0x1c23af28 and 0xacca13fc replay with roles fixed to the original deployer or to the CREATE2 deployer itself. 0x3a3a9a07, 0x74803bd5 and 0x4440854b cannot be rebuilt on Unichain by a stranger because a factory or an implementation they need was made by a plain CREATE from one key (type 2 transactions with chainId 1), and that key has nonce 0 on Unichain. No constructor that was run reads ORIGIN or leaves an open initializer, so no stranger gains a role (Task 3 empty), and CREATE2 address derivation matches Ethereum on the 11 networks where a replay was simulated. Core reads no hook code at initialize (src/PoolManager.sol:117-126, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-127), which is why these pools exist. The 13 hooks with code only on Robinhood Chain, BNB Smart Chain or Arc were not traced (endpoint limits) and are left as a low lead; their pools hold no liquidity.
